title: TemplateSection.removeTemplate clears customer lookup with `dcfg_customer_id: null` â€” wrong payload shape
detail: Line 2104: `await apiPatch(`/${EntitySets.docTemplates}(${tplId})`, { dcfg_customer_id: null });` â€” this will not clear the customer lookup. To null a Dataverse lookup via Power Pages you must either PATCH with `{ 'dcfg_customer_id@odata.bind': null }` (same bind-name form the code uses to set it on line 2091) or DELETE the `/entity(id)/dcfg_customer_id/$ref`. Sending `dcfg_customer_id: null` as a plain property either throws 400 or is silently ignored. TemplateDetail.jsx line 641 uses the correct `'dcfg_customer_id@odata.bind': null` form. Net effect on the Admin â†’ Customer Config â†’ Custom Templates tab: 'Remove' button appears to succeed but the template stays linked to the customer.
evidence: Admin.jsx:2100-2108 removeTemplate function; compare to TemplateDetail.jsx:641 which uses the correct null-bind form.
recommendedFix: Change line 2104 to `await apiPatch(`/${EntitySets.docTemplates}(${tplId})`, { 'dcfg_customer_id@odata.bind': null });`. Same pattern as TemplateDetail.jsx:641.

title: TRADE_OPTIONS constant declared inside CostCodeForm â€” re-created on every render
detail: Line 891: `const TRADE_OPTIONS = [ ... ];` is declared inside the CostCodeForm component body, so a new array and 13 new option-objects are allocated every time the form re-renders. Not a performance hot path (form is short-lived) but the pattern is inconsistent with the module-level SECTIONS/NAV_ROUTES constants at the top of the file. Low priority.
evidence: Admin.jsx:891-905 â€” TRADE_OPTIONS inside function CostCodeForm.
recommendedFix: Hoist TRADE_OPTIONS out of CostCodeForm to module scope (near the other top-of-file constants).

title: DocumentTemplatesTab load + save errors only console.error â€” no user feedback
detail: Line 206 `catch (e) { console.error('Load templates:', e); }` and line 229 `catch (e) { console.error('Save template:', e); }` â€” same pattern repeats for OnboardingStepsTab (424, 447), LocationTypesTab (667, 688), CostCodesTab (802, 823), ApplianceTypesTab (977, 998), VendorsTab (1136, 1157), and IntakeFieldsTab (1587, 1631). Most of these tabs don't import or use useToast, so a save failure leaves the form frozen with no indication to the admin that anything went wrong. The Customer Config tabs (BlanketSection, APMappingSection, TemplateSection) DO use toast.show correctly â€” those are the template for the pattern. Impact: any transient 401/403/500 during an admin edit silently fails; admin thinks the save worked and leaves.
evidence: Admin.jsx:195 (DocumentTemplatesTab) imports no toast; catches only log to console. Compare to CustomerConfigTab children which `const toast = useToast()` and show errors via toast.
recommendedFix: Add `const toast = useToast();` at the top of every tab component that lacks one (DocumentTemplatesTab, OnboardingStepsTab, LocationTypesTab, CostCodesTab, ApplianceTypesTab, VendorsTab, IntakeFieldsTab). Replace the `catch (e) { console.error(...); }` blocks with `catch (e) { console.error(...); toast.show('err', 'Failed to save â€” ' + e.message); }`. Same fix in load-error handlers.

title: Admin screen has no in-component isAdmin check â€” relies entirely on route-level guard
detail: Admin.jsx destructures `const { user } = usePortalUser()` at line 97 but never calls isAdmin() or gates anything by role. Every tab (including Customer Config + AP Mappings which PATCH lookups, and Navigation which writes site config) is visible and editable to any user who reaches the /admin route. This works today because CR-2026-04-09-0219 added a RoleGuard wrapper on the /admin route in AppRouter.jsx (batch 01 fix). But defense-in-depth suggests the component itself should verify admin role before rendering â€” especially since the non-admin fallback currently relies on NavPanel hiding the /admin link and RoleGuard redirecting. If the router guard is ever removed or bypassed, every admin action is exposed.
evidence: Admin.jsx:97 `const { user } = usePortalUser();` â€” isAdmin/isManager are NOT destructured.
recommendedFix:
Destructure isAdmin from usePortalUser and render an access-denied fallback if isAdmin() is false: `const { user, isAdmin } = usePortalUser(); if (!isAdmin()) return
Admin access required
;`. Low priority given the route-level guard, but improves defense-in-depth.

title: Admin VendorsTab $select includes `dcfg_trade` â€” same singular vs plural uncertainty as Directory/VendorList
detail: Line 1134: `$select=...` â€” but actually no, line 1134 lists the known columns and the `dcfg_trade` is NOT in it. Actually re-reading: `dcfg_vendorid,dcfg_legal_name,dcfg_display_name,dcfg_address,dcfg_city,dcfg_state,dcfg_zip,dcfg_phone,dcfg_email,dcfg_primary_contact,dcfg_signer_name,dcfg_signer_title,dcfg_payment_terms,dcfg_payment_process,dcfg_active_flag`. No trade column in the Admin list. Category 8a $select-safety: dcfg_vendor is not in the four explicit-list tables, so this is not a 8a violation, but the VendorsTab form (line 1217) doesn't capture trade either. So the admin vendor management surface has no trade field â€” consistent internally but inconsistent with VendorList/Directory which both try to display it. Catalog-only note.
evidence: Admin.jsx:1134 VendorsTab $select lacks trade. VendorList.jsx:74 and Directory.jsx:68 include `dcfg_trade`. Compare to ProjectList.jsx:25 which maintains a hardcoded TRADES constant (frontend list).
recommendedFix: Decision needed: if vendors have trades at all, Admin should capture it. If dcfg_vendor.dcfg_trades is the real column, add it to Admin VendorsTab $select and form. Align Directory and VendorList to the same name. No code change in this file alone â€” cross-cutting.
